rationale: This empirical study uses spatial lag regression models to evaluate the effects of federal public investment spending on private capital accumulation, earnings, nonfarm employment growth and county-level economic development in Appalachia during the 1980s and 1990s. It does not address household or community water or sanitation service access (Criterion 1), water/sanitation legal or administrative rules (Criterion 2), or water/sanitation access outcomes (Criterion 4). Primary exclusion code: E01 (wrong topic).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both the narrow and plain readings of Criterion 2 because the study is entirely outside the water and sanitation domain (E01), examining aggregate federal public investment spending, private capital accumulation and county economic development in Appalachia.

evidence_quotes.quote: This analysis examines the relationship between federal public investment spending and economic development in the special case of Appalachia.
However, while federal public investment spending has positive effects on measures of private capital accumulation, it has no direct effect on measures of economic development.
